note: Layout migration, not content generation. Each fixture is a project at a different stack-it format; the skill must detect the format, restructure only the files the hop calls for, and leave every human-written byte alone. Format 2 splits the agent-facing reference in two: docs/stack.md, the small file every agent loads through the AGENTS.md pointer, and docs/stack-notes.md, the one read on demand. migrate never generates or refreshes stack content: the most it writes is the old CLAUDE.md text moved into docs/stack-notes.md, inside that file's markers on the 1 to 2 hop and below its end marker when the file already exists, plus one-line stubs where nothing moved, so the AGENTS.md pointer always resolves and docs/stack.md always points at a notes file that exists. document-stack regenerates all of it. The writes are ordered destination before source: both docs files are written before the block is cut from CLAUDE.md. Nothing is ever appended to docs/stack.md's tail; carried text belongs in the notes tier. There is exactly one hop, 1 to 2: the intermediate 0.5.x layouts (a docs/stack.md with no markers, a single-file reference) are unsupported, nothing migrates from them, and an owned docs file with no markers stops the run instead. Fixtures for stop cases (broken-markers, invalid-lockfile) hold only the files that trigger the stop, since the checks halt the hop before any write.

evals.name: v1-with-lockfile-accept-import
evals.prompt: My stack-it files are in the old format. Bring them up to date with the new layout. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Two signals are readable and both say 1: .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml has no format key, and CLAUDE.md carries the marker block. There is no docs/stack.md and no docs/stack-notes.md, so the highest signal is 1. All three checks run BEFORE any write: the lockfile validates, the CLAUDE.md markers are a clean single pair, and AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md resolve to ordinary separate files. Then the writes, in order: (a) stack.yaml gains 'format: 2' as the first top-level key with the rest of the file (key order, stack list order, notes, caveats) unchanged, and revalidates. (b) BOTH docs files are written. docs/stack.md is a stub: the header '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives. Rationale, wiring, and carried notes live in docs/stack-notes.md.', a blank line, then one marker pair holding 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.' and the plain-path pointer sentence 'Detail for every pin, the wiring, and the notes carried forward from earlier docs: docs/stack-notes.md. Read it before changing configuration or adding a tool.' with NO '@' before the path. docs/stack-notes.md takes the block's text, CARRIED even though the lockfile exists and validated: a lockfile's fields are structured (tool, version, install steps, caveats, a free-form notes string) and plenty of what a human typed into that block fits none of them, so anything the new render will not state lives nowhere else. That file is the header '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2, notes tier. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives.', a blank line, then one marker pair whose first line is 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.' followed by the carried content. Exactly one 'Generated by' line per file, no old markers inside the carried text, and carried headings promoted one level ('## Tech Stack' becomes '# Tech Stack', '### Commands' becomes '## Commands'). Nothing is written below either end marker. (c) ONLY THEN is the whole marker block removed from CLAUDE.md, along with one surrounding blank line, leaving no double blank; the House rules and Deployment notes sections survive byte for byte. Cutting before the destinations exist is a failure even when the end state looks the same. (d) AGENTS.md is created containing exactly the pointer line 'Before adding a dependency or running the build, test, or lint toolchain, read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md', with the path NOT in backticks, no HTML markers, and no second line for the notes file, and it resolves, because docs/stack.md now exists. (e) CLAUDE.md still has human prose, so the skill asks once and, on this yes, adds the single line '@AGENTS.md' at the top and nothing else. (f) README.md is untouched, markers and all. No stack content is generated anywhere, so the report says docs/stack-notes.md holds the carried text, docs/stack.md holds a stub, and document-stack runs next to regenerate both, and it ends with 'migrated to 2'. Two failures this pins: dropping the block because a lockfile exists, and putting the carried text in docs/stack.md, the file every session loads.

evals.name: v1-with-lockfile-decline-import
evals.prompt: My stack-it files are in the old format. Bring them up to date with the new layout. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is no. Then run it once more. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Same detection, same three checks before any write, and the same write order as the accept case, including both docs files written before anything is cut from CLAUDE.md, the block carried into docs/stack-notes.md under the 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.' line and docs/stack.md written as the stub with its plain-path pointer, except the bridge: the user declines the '@AGENTS.md' import, so the skill appends the pointer line 'Before adding a dependency or running the build, test, or lint toolchain, read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md' to CLAUDE.md instead, with no markers, no '@AGENTS.md' line, and a blank line before it. Claude Code still reaches docs/stack.md, one hop instead of two, and the file it points at exists and points at a notes file that exists. The report lists CLAUDE.md under what CHANGED, not under what was left alone, says both docs files are migrate's placeholders and that document-stack runs next, and ends with 'migrated to 2'. The second run reads format 2 off the docs/stack.md header, verifies the layout, finds every piece in place including docs/stack-notes.md, and changes nothing: it must not re-ask about the import, must not append a second pointer line, and must leave both already-present docs files byte for byte. It should also say both sections are still migrate placeholders and that document-stack has not filled them in.

evals.name: v1-no-lockfile
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Only one signal is readable, the CLAUDE.md start marker, so the format is 1. There is no docs/stack.md, no docs/stack-notes.md and no .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml. With no lockfile the removed block is the only record of the (inferred) stack, and it is carried the same way it would be with one. docs/stack-notes.md ends up as the header line '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2, notes tier. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives.', a blank line, then a single <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> pair whose first line inside the start marker is 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.', a blank line, then the carried content. docs/stack.md ends up as the format 2 header, a blank line, and one marker pair holding 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.' plus the plain-path pointer sentence to docs/stack-notes.md, no '@' anywhere near the path. Exactly one 'Generated by' line per file: the block's own banner is dropped with the markers. No old stack-it markers survive inside the carried text. Carried headings are promoted one level ('## Tech Stack' becomes '# Tech Stack', '### Commands' becomes '## Commands'). Nothing is written below either end marker; the notes tail is document-stack's to fill when it carries notes forward, and docs/stack.md's tail is never written to at all. Both files are written BEFORE the block is cut. CLAUDE.md then keeps House rules and Deployment notes verbatim with the block and one blank line gone, and since the user said yes it also starts with the single line '@AGENTS.md'; AGENTS.md is created with the single pointer line; no lockfile is created or stamped (the skill must not fabricate a stack.yaml, and there is nothing to stamp); README.md is untouched. The report calls both files placeholders that document-stack will regenerate and ends with 'migrated to 2'.

evals.name: already-current
evals.prompt: Can you migrate my stack-it artifacts to the latest layout? The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Detects format 2 from the docs/stack.md header, then verifies the layout is actually complete: no marker block in CLAUDE.md, docs/stack.md present with one clean marker pair, docs/stack-notes.md present with one clean marker pair, the pointer present in AGENTS.md, the bridge present, the format stamp present in stack.yaml. All of it holds, so it reports the project is current and changes NOTHING: no duplicate pointer line appended to AGENTS.md (it already contains @docs/stack.md, plus human-written house rules and deployment notes that stay verbatim), no edit to the one-line @AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md, no rewrite of either docs file, no second 'format: 2' key in stack.yaml, no touching the README block. BOTH tails are untouched: the '## Local overrides' line below the end marker in docs/stack.md and the '## Team notes' section below the end marker in docs/stack-notes.md. So are both generated sections: this skill never rewrites either, current or not. The sections hold real content rather than a migrate line, so there is nothing to flag about document-stack not having run. Says what it checked and that there was nothing to do; a no-op run must be safe and obviously a no-op. The report ends with the line 'migrated to 2' verbatim, so a caller can parse the outcome.

evals.name: v1-block-only
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md is nothing but the marker block: there is no human prose to preserve. The lockfile exists and validates, and the block's text is still carried into docs/stack-notes.md: its notes-tier header line, then one marker pair whose first line is 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.', then the carried content with its headings promoted one level and its own banner dropped. docs/stack.md is written alongside it as the stub, header plus one marker pair holding the placeholder line and the plain-path pointer to the notes file. Only then does the cut run, and after it CLAUDE.md holds nothing but whitespace, so the bridge case 'doesn't exist, or holds nothing but whitespace' matches and the skill writes the single line '@AGENTS.md' WITHOUT asking. CLAUDE.md ends as exactly '@AGENTS.md' and nothing else. AGENTS.md is created with the pointer line and resolves, stack.yaml is stamped 'format: 2', the README is untouched, and the report says docs/stack-notes.md holds the carried text and docs/stack.md a stub, that document-stack runs next, and ends with 'migrated to 2'. Two failures this pins: asking the user about the bridge here, and dropping the block because a lockfile exists.

evals.name: broken-markers
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md has a '<!-- stack-it:stack start -->' with NO matching end marker, so where the generated block stops is unknowable. The format still reads 1 from the lockfile's missing key and from the marker itself, but marker integrity is check 2 and it fails, so the skill stops BEFORE the first write. Nothing at all changed: no text cut from CLAUDE.md, no format stamp on stack.yaml (the stamp is the first write and never runs), no docs/stack.md, no docs/stack-notes.md, no AGENTS.md, no bridge. It shows the user the offending lines and ends with 'stopped: <reason>'. Two failures this pins: guessing the end of the block or deleting to end of file, and leaving a half-migrated tree because a check ran after a write.

evals.name: invalid-lockfile
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Check 1 runs before any write and fails with three problems: stack[0].version is the unquoted float 3.14, stack[1].install is an empty list, stack[2].choice is missing. The skill reports the validator's output verbatim and stops with NO edits: the CLAUDE.md block stays, no format stamp on stack.yaml, no docs/stack.md, no docs/stack-notes.md, no AGENTS.md, no bridge. It must not fix the lockfile, and it must not treat the failure as 'no usable lockfile' and run the hop around it: a lockfile that merely needs repair is not permission to restructure the project. Ends with 'stopped: <reason>'.

evals.name: unstamped-no-block
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The lockfile has no format key and there is nothing else to read: no docs/stack.md, no docs/stack-notes.md, no CLAUDE.md at all, so no marker block. A missing key reads as 1, which is behind, so the hop runs. This is a project that ran decide-stack on an older stack-it and never document-stack. Check 1 passes (the lockfile validates), check 2 finds no markers, which is not a failure but simply no block to cut, and check 3 has no symlinks to resolve. Writes: stack.yaml is stamped 'format: 2' as the first top-level key and revalidates; with nothing to carry, BOTH docs files are stubs. docs/stack.md is the header '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives. Rationale, wiring, and carried notes live in docs/stack-notes.md.', a blank line, and one marker pair holding 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.' (not the 'Moved from CLAUDE.md' line, since nothing moved) followed by the plain-path pointer sentence to docs/stack-notes.md, with no '@' before the path. docs/stack-notes.md is its notes-tier header, a blank line, and one marker pair holding the same 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.' line and nothing else. The cut is skipped; AGENTS.md is created with the single pointer line, which resolves; CLAUDE.md does not exist, so the bridge case creates it containing exactly '@AGENTS.md', with no ask. README.md is untouched. The report says both docs files hold stubs and that document-stack runs next to fill them in, and ends with 'migrated to 2'. Two half-states this pins: no docs/stack.md at all, so the fresh pointer aims at a missing file, and a docs/stack.md whose pointer aims at a docs/stack-notes.md that was never written.

evals.name: v2-leftover-block
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The lockfile is stamped 'format: 2' and both docs files carry format 2 headers, so the project is already on the current layout; but CLAUDE.md still holds a '<!-- stack-it:stack start/end -->' block, left behind by a migration that did not finish. Layout verification catches it. The block's text must NOT go inside the markers of either docs file: those sections belong to document-stack and are regenerated on every run, so anything written there is lost on the next pass. It must not go into docs/stack.md's tail either, since that file is loaded at every session start. Instead, subject to marker integrity on all three files, its content is appended BELOW the end marker of docs/stack-notes.md under its '## Notes carried forward' heading, preceded by the single provenance line 'Carried forward by stack-it. Each line says something the generated section above did not; prune what the section grows to cover.' The hygiene differs from the 1 to 2 hop on one point: the block's own '> Generated by stack-it's document-stack' banner and its old markers are dropped as always, but its headings are NOT promoted. Heading promotion is for text moving into a file of its own inside the markers; a tail append sets scaffolding aside exactly as document-stack does, so '## Tech Stack', '### Commands' and '### Gotchas' are dropped and only bullets land under '## Notes carried forward'. A promoted '# Tech Stack' appearing in that tail is a failure. The '### Gotchas' note about uv rebuilding the venv after a pyproject edit is the line that matters; it exists in no lockfile field, and it lands as a plain bullet with no heading above it. That tail already holds a '## Notes carried forward' heading, its provenance line, and one earlier note about DATABASE_URL: heading and line are reused, never doubled, the earlier note stays where it is, and the uv gotcha is appended after it. Block lines either generated section already states (Python 3.14.3, FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, the 'uv run pytest' command) are set aside and never appended, so the provenance line stays true. Only after that write does the block come out of CLAUDE.md, leaving the file as exactly '@AGENTS.md'. Both generated sections are byte for byte what they were, docs/stack.md is untouched end to end including its empty tail, AGENTS.md and stack.yaml are untouched, no second 'format: 2' key appears, and the report names the repair it re-ran and lists what it carried. Three failures this pins: writing into a managed section, appending to docs/stack.md instead of the notes tier, and cutting the block without carrying it because the lockfile could regenerate the tools.

evals.name: stamped-lockfile-only
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The only file present is .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml, stamped 'format: 2'. There is no docs/stack.md, no docs/stack-notes.md, no AGENTS.md and no CLAUDE.md, which is not a broken layout: this project was decided and locked but never documented. So there is nothing to repair and nothing to migrate. The skill changes NOTHING: it does not write a stub in either docs file, does not create the pointer, does not create the bridge, does not restamp the lockfile. It says the layout is current for what exists, that the project has not been documented yet, and that document-stack is the skill to run next, which will write all of those files itself. The closing line must say both docs files are ABSENT, not that they hold stubs: this run wrote neither, and a report that points at content it did not write sends the user to a file that isn't there. Writing stubs and a pointer here is the failure this pins: migrate would be inventing a documentation stage the user never reached.

evals.name: notes-missing-beside-owned-stack-md
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: A format-2 project with one piece gone. docs/stack.md is present, ours, well formed, holds a real generated section with the plain-path pointer sentence to docs/stack-notes.md, and carries a '## Local overrides' tail; the lockfile is stamped 'format: 2'; AGENTS.md has the pointer and CLAUDE.md is the '@AGENTS.md' bridge. Only docs/stack-notes.md is missing, so the pointer inside docs/stack.md resolves to nothing. Layout verification catches it, and this is a missing piece rather than a never-documented project: docs/stack.md exists, which is what separates this from the stamped-lockfile-only case. Marker integrity runs on docs/stack.md first, since it is present and owned, and it passes. Then the one missing piece is repaired by re-running only the write step that produces it: docs/stack-notes.md is created as the header '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2, notes tier. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives.', a blank line, and one marker pair holding the single line 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.' Nothing else is touched: docs/stack.md is byte for byte what it was, section and '## Local overrides' tail alike, because an owned docs file that is already there is never rewritten and its content is document-stack's anyway; AGENTS.md gets no second pointer line; CLAUDE.md is not edited; stack.yaml gains no second 'format: 2' key; the README is untouched. The report names the one step it re-ran, says docs/stack-notes.md is a stub for document-stack to fill in, and ends with 'migrated to 2'. Two failures this pins: treating a missing notes file as a stop, and rewriting docs/stack.md while repairing its sibling.

evals.name: stack-missing-beside-owned-notes
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The mirror of notes-missing-beside-owned-stack-md, on the other tier. docs/stack-notes.md is present, ours, well formed, holds a real generated section and a '## Team notes' tail; the lockfile is stamped 'format: 2'; AGENTS.md carries the pointer and CLAUDE.md is the '@AGENTS.md' bridge. docs/stack.md is GONE, so the AGENTS.md pointer resolves to nothing and no agent reaches the reference at all. Ownership runs first and passes on the one docs file that exists, then marker integrity passes on it too, then layout verification finds the missing piece. This is a repair rather than a never-documented project: docs/stack-notes.md exists, which is what separates it from the stamped-lockfile-only case. Re-run only write step 2's stack.md half: docs/stack.md is created as the header '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives. Rationale, wiring, and carried notes live in docs/stack-notes.md.', a blank line, and one marker pair holding 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.' followed by the plain-path pointer sentence 'Detail for every pin, the wiring, and the notes carried forward from earlier docs: docs/stack-notes.md. Read it before changing configuration or adding a tool.', with no '@' before the path. The pointer resolves again and the restored file points at a notes file that exists. Nothing else is touched: docs/stack-notes.md is byte for byte what it was, section and '## Team notes' tail alike, because its content is document-stack's and an owned docs file that is already there is never rewritten; AGENTS.md gets no second pointer line; CLAUDE.md is not edited; stack.yaml gains no second 'format: 2' key; the README is untouched. The report names the one step it re-ran, says docs/stack.md is a stub for document-stack to fill in, and ends with 'migrated to 2'. Two failures this pins: regenerating a stack.md section from the notes file that survived, which would be migrate writing content, and rewriting the notes file while repairing its sibling.
